scientific_question: On the untouched NIST ENSO monthly pressure dataset, can the frozen external coverage driver and scope-aware adapter evaluate a cubic/cubic candidate, continuous ellipsoid safety, pointwise residual bounds and bound composition without protocol drift or native-periodic-model overclaim?

dataset_scope.name: NIST/ITL StRD ENSO
dataset_scope.native_model: Nine-parameter miscellaneous Fourier class with annual and two longer cycles; the cubic/cubic rational candidate is an approximation stress test, not the native model
dataset_scope.native_equation: y = b1 + b2*cos(2*pi*x/12) + b3*sin(2*pi*x/12) + b5*cos(2*pi*x/b4) + b6*sin(2*pi*x/b4) + b8*cos(2*pi*x/b7) + b9*sin(2*pi*x/b7) + e
dataset_scope.response: monthly averaged atmospheric pressure difference between Easter Island and Darwin, Australia
dataset_scope.reference: Kahaner, D., C. Moler, and S. Nash (1989), Numerical Methods and Software, pp. 441-445
dataset_scope.model_family_scope: The native periodic model differs from previous candidate families, but this reanalysis is not an independent physical experiment or validation of the native ENSO model

implementation_rule.changes_after_freeze: No driver, scope adapter or wrapper change is permitted under this protocol; any implementation change requires a new protocol and preservation of this frozen analysis
implementation_rule.scope_rule: The adapter applies the frozen ENSO-specific limitation and records both wrapper and adapter hashes; it does not alter fitting, certificates, bounds or thresholds

candidate_rule.optimizer: scipy.optimize.curve_fit method=lm, maxfev=200000, full_output=true; select lowest training RSS
candidate_rule.scope_limitation: The cubic/cubic candidate is only an approximation stress test and not the native ENSO nine-parameter Fourier model with annual, El Nino and Southern Oscillation cycles; periodic predictive skill and deterministic denominator certification are separate evidence axes
candidate_rule.retuning: No model, start, radius, fold or threshold changes after seeing outcomes

fold_rule.construction: Sort unique x values into five contiguous, nearly equal groups; repeated x never crosses fitting and test sets; every observation is evaluated once
fold_rule.baseline: Cubic polynomial fitted only on the other four groups; this is a candidate baseline, not the native nine-parameter Fourier fit

ellipsoid_rule.radius_scope: Fixed before fitting; a deterministic scale only, not a confidence level
ellipsoid_rule.covariance: Use denominator block from the best training attempt; require exact symmetry and positive definiteness
ellipsoid_rule.continuous_certificate: Require exact D^2-rho^2*z^T*Sigma*z>0 and sign-consistent D over each closed held-out interval
ellipsoid_rule.pointwise_bound: For R=rho*sqrt_upper(z^T Sigma z), require |D|-R>0 and compute prediction shift and observed residual upper bounds; compare with the independent box at the same radius
ellipsoid_rule.coverage: Check actual |y-f_snapshot| against each available deterministic residual bound and record any violation; do not call this probability calibration
ellipsoid_rule.composition: For each available point, preserve actual residual, prediction shift and residual upper bound so shift share can be audited without refitting

prohibitions: No claim that the native ENSO model is cubic/cubic or that the candidate captures the physical El Nino and Southern Oscillation mechanisms
No description of this reanalysis as a newly performed independent physical experiment or native model-family validation
No hiding of optimizer failures, non-positive covariance, unavailable bounds, coverage violations or prediction failures
No probability, confidence, RMSE-bound or continuous-x error-bound claim from pointwise bounds
No use of the original nine-parameter certified fit as candidate holdout evidence
No retuning of starts, radius, folds or candidate degree after seeing candidate outcomes
